workflow: 4x4 cardinal-mask sprite sheet on a flat chroma-key background

asset.prompt: Create a production-ready pixel-art sprite sheet for a top-down 2D game building. Use Image 1 for the warm golden-brown log palette, dark brown outline, cut-log end grain, and chunky pixel language. Use Image 2 for the game's compact top-down building perspective, shading density, and scale. Asset: a simple wooden fence / crossed-log barricade that nearly fills one 1x1 tile. The core is made from sturdy crossed logs and pointed timber stakes. It must read clearly at 32x32 pixels. Layout: one perfectly square 4-by-4 sprite sheet, 16 equal square cells, row-major frame indices 0 through 15. Every frame depicts the same central barricade with cardinal connector arms controlled by this exact bitmask: north/up=1, east/right=2, south/down=4, west/left=8; frame number equals mask. Thus frame 0 has no connector, frame 1 north only, frame 2 east only, frame 3 north+east, continuing exactly through frame 15 with all four. Connector arms must reach the exact center of the corresponding cell edge and only those edges. Keep the central crossed-log construction, palette, outline thickness, lighting direction, and visual weight identical across all 16 cells. Composition: isolated game sprite sheet, orthographic three-quarter top-down pixel art, readable silhouette, thick 1-2 pixel dark outline at final 32x32 scale, subject uses about 30-32 pixels of each cell, no perspective drift between frames. Wood only, no metal, no foliage. Background: perfectly uniform flat chroma-key magenta #FF00FF covering every non-sprite pixel. No transparency, no shadow outside the object, no checkerboard, no cell borders. Hard constraints: no text, no numbers, no labels, no guides, no grid lines, no UI, no watermark, no antialiasing, no gradients, no blur, no glow, no extra objects. Exact 4x4 arrangement, equal cells, consistent registration.
